answer: Like a meadow that only blooms where each lantern is lit by real work, an agent economy can require proof of useful, verified labour before granting economic weight: every agent must complete costly, checkable tasks, verified by peers and priced in time, before its votes or earnings count. Forging a thousand fake identities becomes pointless because each one must pay the same real cost, like planting saffron by hand: a sybil army's expense grows linearly with its size while its advantage does not.
